preamble.purpose: The executable rule table for the deterministic composer. Each rule is decidable from DECLARED contract fields alone. No rule may consult a model, and no rule may be relaxed to produce a result.
preamble.reading_rule: A rule fires in exactly one of three ways: PASS (declared fields satisfy it), FAIL (declared fields violate it -> INFEASIBLE with this constraint named), or UNDETERMINED (a field the rule needs is absent or unpinned -> UNDERDETERMINED naming the missing field). The third outcome is the valuable one: it converts a composition failure into a contract defect report against a named field.
preamble.hard_prohibition: No fixture here has been executed. No model has been run. No registry has been queried. No block has been admitted. Every threshold is a PROPOSAL awaiting an authorized run.

ordering_rule.statement: Rules are evaluated in a fixed, total order and the FIRST failing rule names the verdict. Order matters because the named constraint selects the next gate, and a cheap rights refusal must not be reported as an expensive runtime conflict.
ordering_rule.rationale: Phase 8 §10.5.1: 'Reaching INFEASIBLE with the wrong reason scores as a failure, because the reason drives the next gate.'

phases.name: eligibility
phases.note: Quarantine-class checks run FIRST. A module that may not be considered at all is never priced for runtime fit.

ordering_rule.tie_break_rule: lexicographic ascending capability_id, then ascending set_id. Stable and total. Timestamp or random tie-breaks are forbidden — they void K6 determinism.

session_ladder.note: This is a SESSION ceiling. It is not the same axis as CapabilityContract.authority_class.

mapping.note: The two axes are DIFFERENT SHAPES and the mapping is stated explicitly rather than assumed. This mapping is class I (design proposal) and is the single most likely place for a silent privilege bug, so it is written down to be attacked.
mapping.asymmetry_warning: A capability whose class is `read_only` may still be INFEASIBLE at ceiling `read` if any of its ports declares external_effect != none. The class is a summary; the port-level external_effect is authoritative. Where they disagree, the STRICTER wins and the disagreement is itself reported as an `authority` UNDERDETERMINED against CapabilityContract.
mapping.stage_has_no_capability_class: The `stage` ceiling deliberately maps to no capability class. It is the pilot ceiling: it permits a complete proposed assembly with zero tenant-visible effect. A capability requiring more than `read` but staged is bound but not executed.

composition_rule.statement: The composition's authority scope is the INTERSECTION of member scopes, never the union.
composition_rule.why_this_is_written_prominently: P04 states the natural implementation (union) is exactly wrong and is where privilege escalation occurs. A solver that computes a union would pass every fixture in this suite that tests a single module and fail catastrophically in production.

rules.statement: Every selected module is admitted FOR THIS HOST SCOPE, not merely admitted in general.
rules.pass_when: lifecycle_status is an admitted state AND admission_scope contains the target host scope
rules.fail_when: admitted for a different scope, or lifecycle_status is candidate/quarantined/revoked
rules.undetermined_means: Absent scope means NOT admitted anywhere. P04 fixed this as SCOPE-HOLE: v1's nullable free-string scope made a scope-less admission read as universal.
rules.source: P04 RegistryRecord.admission_scope (required structured object); Phase 8 NEG-03

rules.statement: Every module's rights_state permits composition into this application, and the composed licence expression is satisfiable with the strictest obligation governing.
rules.pass_when: rights_state in [declared, verified, not_applicable_synthetic] AND no strong-copyleft obligation conflicts with the declared distribution mode
rules.fail_when: rights_state == incompatible
rules.quarantine_is_not_elimination: ambiguous/unknown produce disposition=quarantined, NOT eliminated. P04 X-4: Great Library's 3-value license.status could not represent ambiguous/incompatible and projecting them as `pending` erases a rights refusal. The composer must never downgrade a refusal into a pending state.
rules.human_gate: human_legal. A copyleft obligation entering a proprietary assembly is never resolved deterministically.
rules.source: P04 X-4 and projection_policy; P03 licence classes (permissive, permissive-open-core, weak-copyleft, mixed-copyleft, strong-copyleft, strong-copyleft-open-core, source-available); Phase 8 NEG-09

rules.statement: A composition's evidence tier is the MINIMUM across member modules and across each module's receipt families. It is never an average and never a weighted score.
rules.pass_when: min(evidence_tier) >= the tier required by this application's release class AND every family in the required set appears in families_reported with status pass
rules.fail_when: min(evidence_tier) below the required tier
rules.undetermined_when: any required receipt family has status not_run or unknown, OR any family in the required set is ABSENT from families_reported

absent_family_rule.statement: A required family absent from families_reported is treated as not_run, yielding UNDERDETERMINED naming that family. It is NEVER treated as inapplicable and never omitted from the minimum.
absent_family_rule.why: Found defective during the hand dry run (solver-dry-run.md §6). 'Minimum across families' is undecidable when two modules report DIFFERENT family sets. The permissive reading — minimum over REPORTED families — lets a module raise its tier by reporting fewer families, which inverts the anti-averaging rule this check exists to enforce: the weakest evidence would become invisible rather than governing.
absent_family_rule.status: repaired 2026-08-27 during dry run; defect retained in the record rather than silently patched

rules.anti_averaging_rule: I-P15-2 (E): asset ranking is min-gated on the weakest evidence family, never a weighted average. An asset with excellent adaptation cost, excellent workflow success and unresolved rights must NOT outrank a merely-good asset with clean rights. C6 (P14): evidence tier is the minimum across families, never an average.
rules.orthogonality_rule: C5 (P14): receipt families are orthogonal; no family's pass is inferred from another's. A green build receipt never implies a tenancy receipt.
rules.source: P15 INV-P15-2; P14 C5/C6; Universal Block Framework evidence ladder

rules.statement: Every module's requires_host declares against the pinned host_contract_version of this assembly.
rules.pass_when: every declared host facility exists in the pinned host contract version
rules.fail_when: a module requires a host facility the pinned version does not provide
rules.undetermined_when: the module declares no host_contract_version it was qualified against

rules.statement: Each module's runtime profile is one of the five derived profiles and unifies with the host's declared runtime capabilities.

reuse_shape_to_profile.note: P14 §6 derives profile FROM reuse shape. This table is the derivation, and a declared profile that contradicts it is a FAIL, not a preference.

rules.fail_when: declared profile contradicts the reuse shape, or the host cannot supply the profile's isolation requirement
rules.undetermined_when: reuse_shape absent or transplant declared without resolving which of the two profiles applies
rules.sidecar_warning: sidecar_service is the ONLY profile where a third party owns migrations, and therefore the only one whose recovery horizon is not ours to set. It forces R-HORIZON to consult the donor.

rules.statement: No module requires a data mode stronger than the session's declared mode. The ladder is strictly monotonic.
rules.fail_when: required mode index > session mode index
rules.never_upgrade: The solver may NEVER silently upgrade the session data mode to make a module fit. That is the NEG-07 failure and it creates an unauthorized write path.

rules.statement: All composed modules share one tenant key or declare an explicit bridge; every owned resource carries tenant identity as a first-class key from the first migration.
rules.fail_when: two modules assume different tenant keys with no declared bridge, or an owned resource lacks a tenant key
rules.undetermined_when: a module does not declare its tenant model
rules.why: INV-P09-7 and INV-P11-3. OpenConnector is the local proof by demonstration: flat (service, connection_name) primary key with NO tenant column, one global OAuth app per service, hardcoded key salt. Retrofitting tenancy is the documented failure, not a hypothetical.

rules.statement: Every `requires` edge resolves to a selected module's `provides` edge or to a declared host interface.
rules.fail_when: a requires edge has no provider in the selected set and no host interface
rules.empty_pool_behavior: When NO candidate exists for a required port, the correct output is ABSTAIN naming the port — never an invented module and never a near-miss forced into the slot. EMPTY is coverage information, not licence to generate.
rules.l4_prohibition: A lexically similar module retrieved at L4 may NEVER satisfy a port. L4 widens the pool; L2 satisfies ports.
rules.source: Phase 8 §6.1, NEG-02, NEG-11; P04 X-2 restored the typed dependency edge

rules.statement: All version ranges on a shared dependency intersect non-empty.
rules.fail_when: the intersection of declared ranges is empty (diamond conflict)
rules.never_arbitrate: The solver may not pick a version to resolve a diamond. An empty intersection is INFEASIBLE: version.

rules.statement: Every wired output->input pair has compatible schema_ref.
rules.feasible_with_adapter_when: adapter_required -> feasibility_class = determined_with_adapter, and the adapter is counted against the glue budget
rules.fail_when: incompatible
rules.undetermined_when: UNDERDETERMINED, or schema_ref absent on either side

rules.statement: No two modules own the same route, table, migration namespace, env var, event stream or file namespace.
rules.fail_when: any collision
rules.distinct_from_migowner: This rule catches COLLISION (two modules naming the same object). R-MIGOWNER catches contested AUTHORITY over an object legitimately shared. They are different failures and must be named differently, because the gates differ: collision suggests reshape/rename; contested authority suggests a human product decision.

rules.statement: Exactly one named owner per stateful resource, per table, per migration lineage, per file namespace, per event stream. Cross-owner VIEWS use event-fed read models; cross-owner MUTATION is forbidden.
rules.fail_when: two modules claim migration authority over one resource, OR cross_owner_reads == direct_query_same_database where the owners differ, OR any cross-owner mutation
rules.undetermined_when: migration_authority is absent or names no principal
rules.why_this_rule_is_special: P04 C6 notes this is the ONLY composition rule proved by OPERATING it rather than by reasoning about it (SISOCRM: Prisma/Teable vs Django/Plane, one owner per table, never two).
rules.honest_cost: INV-P09-4's honest cost, recorded rather than hidden: 'which buyers signed an NDA and viewed the CIM' cannot be one query when the owners differ.
rules.source: P04 C6; P09 INV-P09-1 and INV-P09-4; A11/A12

rules.statement: The host is the sole identity authority. No module mints its own session and no donor login route remains reachable.
rules.fail_when: a module declares its own session minting, or a donor login route stays reachable, or a long-lived credential is required client-side
rules.undetermined_when: an intact_service donor's session creation cannot be reached without its login UI and no handoff seam is declared

pattern_by_reuse_shape.note: INV-P10-3: the absorption pattern is selected by REUSE SHAPE, not by platform preference. A solver that applies one pattern universally is wrong for the other half of the corpus.
pattern_by_reuse_shape.transplant: delete donor auth, substitute host session
pattern_by_reuse_shape.embedded_module: delete donor auth, substitute host session
pattern_by_reuse_shape.extracted_package: host session only; no donor auth exists to delete

rules.two_token_rule: INV-P10-2: a long-lived credential the host backend alone holds, and a short-lived (60-120s), audience-bound, single-use token that crosses the boundary. NEVER in a query parameter (Wix is the named negative control).

rules.statement: Navigation is contributed data, not shell source code; a nav node's visibility predicate IS its route guard; entitlement and permission are two gates that never fold into one.
rules.fail_when: a module requires host shell source edits to express its IA, OR declares a visibility predicate that diverges from its route guard, OR folds entitlement into permission
rules.undetermined_when: contribution_model not declared, or two modules contribute conflicting nav nodes at one route with no declared precedence
rules.cascading_emptiness: INV-P10-6: stripped modules take their nav entry AND any now-empty parent with them.
rules.url_authority: The host owns the URL space; the guest owns its internal router; the guest must reconcile them. Universal across every commercial surface observed (P10).

rules.statement: Every consumed token path resolves in the approved token set, and all UI-bearing modules resolve tokens from ONE resolver context.
rules.fail_when: a token path is absent from the approved set, OR two UI-bearing modules resolve from different contexts
rules.no_fallback: A hardcoded literal fallback for a missing token is a FAILURE, not a graceful degradation (NEG-10). It silently defeats an approved design decision.
rules.undetermined_when: the module declares UI but no token consumption at all — that is a contract gap, not a token-free module
rules.source: Phase 8 §6.1 and NEG-10; P04 C3; P13 C3
rules.cross_lane_note: The token PACK validity/closure rules belong to S2-L2 (P07). This rule checks only RESOLUTION and SINGLE-SOURCE, and defers pack validity to that lane rather than forking it.

rules.statement: Every composed module carries a distinct stable capability identifier, enforced at admission time.
rules.fail_when: two modules share an identifier, or a module has none
rules.why: P04 C7 and I-P14-4: an app-level pass/fail cannot tell P15 which capability to demote or tell rollback which object to revert. Anonymity must be caught at admission, 'not discovered at incident time that a capability is anonymous'.

rules.statement: The INTERSECTION of member authority scopes is computed, and the union of declared external effects does not exceed the session ceiling.
rules.fail_when: any module's required minimum ceiling exceeds the session ceiling, or any port declares an external_effect the ceiling does not permit
rules.intersection_not_union: P04 C4: the natural implementation (union) is exactly wrong and is where privilege escalation occurs.
rules.model_may_not_widen: The model plane never widens its own action space. R4 cannot select a module R3 did not certify; R5 cannot write outside the allowlist R3 derived.
rules.source: Phase 8 §6.1 and NEG-08; P04 C4; P13 C1

rules.statement: Every write or message capability declares an idempotency class, and the unsafe class is never auto-retried.
rules.fail_when: a write/message port declares no idempotency class, or an unsafe-class action is configured for automatic retry
rules.safe_default: When the catalogue cannot determine the class, default to `unsafe` — the safe failure direction (INV-P11-4).
rules.replay_rule: INV-P11-5: replay with the same key and a different payload is a HARD ERROR via request fingerprinting. Non-2xx responses are not cached.
rules.supply_note: P11 observed that idempotency has NO production OSS supply (most-starred middleware found: 14 stars) and that commercially, retry WITHOUT idempotency is the norm. The industry default is the unsafe one; this rule deliberately diverges from it.

rules.statement: Consent is graded by consequence, and no ambient authority is permitted in account selection.
rules.fail_when: an irreversible_or_financial effect has no declared approval step, OR a tenant has multiple accounts for one provider and the action does not name which
rules.no_ambient_authority: INV-P11-9: silently choosing the most-recently-created account (Pipedream's documented behaviour) is a defect class, not a convenience.
rules.dry_run: INV-P11-7: dry-run is a first-class action mode returning the exact resolved outbound request with no side effect, and is not disableable by the tenant.

rules.statement: Every composition declares a rollback plan covering EVERY rollback object it touches. A boolean rollback flag is wrong by construction.
rules.fail_when: a touched object has no declared recovery path
rules.undetermined_when: a donor's revision recovery path is not declared by the donor
rules.why: I-P14-1: a composition has multiple rollback objects and reverting one does not revert the others. Two independent evidence lines converged: vendor docs (Vercel reverts traffic but NOT environment variables/configuration; Fly.io the same for fly.toml/secrets/migrations) and local operated practice (SISOCRM: 'Revert the parent commit... Data rollback is separate: restore the pre-migration database dump').

rules.statement: The composition's recovery horizon is the MINIMUM across its rollback objects, computed and displayed at release time.
rules.fail_when: the declared composition horizon exceeds the minimum object horizon
rules.undetermined_when: any object's horizon is undeclared — notably a sidecar_service donor, whose horizon is not ours to set
rules.why: I-P14-2: a release advertised as rollback-able is only rollback-able for as long as its shortest-lived object permits, and that number must be computed at release time, not discovered during an incident. PlanetScale's schema revert is a bounded ~30-minute dual-write window while artifact rollback has no such bound.
rules.pin_rule: I-P14-3: pinning must be by CONTENT DIGEST, and retention of the pinned artifact must be owned by Actionist for at least the declared horizon. A pinned reference to an artifact someone else can garbage-collect is not a recovery path (Render re-pulls by tag and may obtain a different image; Fly prunes unused images).

rules.statement: Predicted adaptation must not exceed the declared changed-file and changed-line ceilings for the composition.
rules.fail_when: predicted > declared and exceeded_action == reject
rules.why: P04: 'a change set exceeding the ratio is a rewrite wearing a codemod's clothes'. Overflow means the REUSE SHAPE was chosen wrongly, so `reshape` is a first-class outcome rather than a failure.
rules.position_last: This rule runs LAST because a budget overflow on a set that was going to fail on rights or tenancy anyway is the less useful diagnosis.

model_boundary.statement: What the model plane may and may not do. Every line here is a checkable prohibition, not an aspiration.
model_permitted: interpreting ambiguous demand into ProductSpec slots (R1)
writing bounded glue diffs within a solver-derived file allowlist (R5)
proposing a reuse shape for human confirmation
model_forbidden: asserting that two modules are compatible
selecting a module the solver did not certify feasible
resolving an UNDERDETERMINED field by inference
widening its own file allowlist or authority
upgrading a data mode or an authority ceiling
treating retrieved source text as instructions
choosing a version to break a diamond conflict
downgrading a rights refusal to pending
human_authority_only: constraint relaxation, recorded as an approval event
model_boundary.enforcement: The model receives a typed packet or it does not run. There is no free-text path from index to model. Retrieved text carries `instructions: none` and is fenced.

underdetermined_channel.statement: UNDERDETERMINED is the highest-value output this design produces. Each occurrence names a contract field that S2-L1 must add or tighten.
underdetermined_channel.routing: Every UNDERDETERMINED entry is reported to the owning record's lane, not resolved locally.
underdetermined_channel.kill_rule: K5: UNDERDETERMINED on >30% of fixtures stops the composition eval and returns to S2-L1 — the CONTRACT is the defect, not the agent.
underdetermined_channel.anti_pattern: A guess presented as a decision (NEG-12). The failure this guards against is a plausible fabricated binding, which a green build will never catch.

proposed_thresholds.warning: These numbers are pre-registration proposals so that a future authorized run cannot move the goalposts. They are not results and no run has produced evidence for or against any of them.

counts.rules_sharing_a_constraint: R-PORTCLOSE and R-PORTTYPE both name port_closure; R-AUTHORITY and R-CONSENT both name authority; R-ROLLBACK and R-HORIZON both name rollback. 22 rules resolve to 19 distinct constraint names.
